answer: Weight comes only from a chip-timed race finish in a registry. The runner enters under its name, wears a chip, and passes split mats and photo checks, with a garden checkpoint matching bib to face; one finish backs one identity, and a transfer voids it. Each fake costs one voyage of preparation: 120 days of training and a 150-unit fee, so 100 fakes cost 15,000 units. A copied chip fails because splits must advance along the basalt climb at human pace, photos matching at every mat; a stand-in spends its own finish, and a swapped bib revokes both, so a farm needs one real runner per fake.
